 SCADA Reporting: 6 Practical Steps for Better Plant Reports

 Every plant collects millions of historian values, yet managers still ask for a simple shift report by morning. Turning raw tags into clear, trusted reports is where the real value of a control system shows up.

 
 SCADA Reporting 
 SQL Integration 
 Energy Reports 
 Report Triggers 
 




 Operators watch live screens, but supervisors, auditors and planners read reports. Well designed reports pull historian data into summaries that support production, quality, energy and maintenance decisions.


 
 Hello everyone, today we are going to learn how SCADA reporting works, which report types plants use, how SQL connects the historian to business systems and how to calculate an energy per tonne report.


 
 
 

 What Is SCADA Reporting?


 SCADA reporting is the process of turning stored process data, alarms and events into structured summaries such as shift, daily and monthly reports. It sits on top of the data collection layer described in how SCADA systems work .


 Sielco Sistemi groups plant reports into four families: production, quality, energy and maintenance. Each family answers a different question for a different reader.


 
 
 Image credit: Trihedral 
 

 The raw material for every report is the historian, explained in what is a process historian . Compression and sampling settings decide how accurate the report totals will be.


 DCS vendors use a similar layered design, as covered in DCS historian data storage . The report engine reads, aggregates and formats that stored data.

 Four SCADA Reporting Families


 
 Production
 Output, batches, runtime and downtime per shift.
 Best for: daily production meetings
 Output 

 Quality
 Lab results, deviations and batch records.
 Best for: audits and customer claims
 Quality 

 Energy
 Power, steam and fuel per unit of product.
 Best for: cost control
 Energy 

 Maintenance
 Run hours, trips and starts per asset.
 Best for: planned maintenance
 Assets 




 Keep each report short and focused on one reader. A single report that tries to serve everyone usually serves nobody.


 SCADA Reporting Triggers Explained


 
 
 Trigger When It Runs Typical Example 

 Scheduled Fixed time or period Shift, daily and monthly summaries 

 On demand Operator or manager request Report for a chosen date range 

 Event driven A process event occurs Batch end report or trip record 

 



 Sielco Sistemi describes these three trigger types as the core of report automation. Event driven reports are valuable because they capture context at the exact moment something happened.


 SQL Integration and Plant Reports


 According to Sielco Sistemi, SQL integration turns the historian from a closed archive into an open resource for ERP, business intelligence and compliance tools. This matches the level 3 and level 4 link in the ISA 95 automation pyramid .
